Let’s grow — together. 💥 ### **🗓️ Agenda** * **18:00 – 18:30** \| 🍕 Check\-in\, Food\, Drinks & Networking * **18:30 – 18:40** \| 👋 Welcome & 1st Anniversary Opening * **18:40 – 19:10** \| 🎤 **Talk #1:** *From Import-Time Transformation to Query-Time Views: Scaling Product Feed Ingestion with MongoDB and AWS* — **Pedro Henriques** * **19:10 – 19:15** \| 🔄 Transition * **19:15 – 19:45** \| 🎤 **Partner Session:** *MongoDB + OutSystems + AWS: From Document Data to Scalable Agentic Experiences* — **Rodolfo Cardoso** * **19:45 – 20:05** \| ☕ Networking Break * **20:05 – 20:35** \| 🎤 **Talk #2:** *From PDF to Chatbot: A Serverless RAG Journey with AWS and MongoDB Atlas* — **João Folgado** * **20:35 – 20:40** \| 🔄 Transition * **20:40 – 21:10** \| 🎤 **Talk #3:** *Outbox Meets MongoDB: No Event Left Behind* — **João Antunes & João Mendes** * **21:10 – 21:30** \| 🎮 MongoDB Kahoot Challenge & Prize Giveaway * **21:30 – 22:00** \| 🤝 Open Networking & Community Discussions \-\-\-\-\-\-\- **Speaker**: Pedro Henriques **Language**: English **Title**: From Import-Time Transformation to Query-Time Views: Scaling Product Feed Ingestion with MongoDB and AWS Abstract: Product feeds rarely arrive in a consistent format. Each customer publishes product information using different schemas, structures, and conventions, while downstream applications require a standardized product model. In this session, we will explore the architecture of a product feed importer built with Node.js microservices, AWS Lambda, Amazon S3, Amazon SQS, Amazon DynamoDB, and MongoDB. The platform monitors product feed publications in customer environments, imports product data into MongoDB, and makes it available to a bundling API that dynamically generates product bundles based on a requested SKU. A central challenge in the solution was deciding where to transform customer-specific product data into a standardized internal model. Initially, these mappings were applied during ingestion. As feed sizes and transformation complexity increased, this approach began to significantly affect import performance and processing time. We will discuss how the architecture evolved by moving these transformations from the ingestion pipeline into MongoDB views, allowing raw product documents to be stored more quickly while applying the standardized representation at query time. The presentation will cover the motivations behind this decision, the resulting trade-offs between write-time and read-time processing, the role of MongoDB views in the solution, and the lessons learned when balancing ingestion performance, query complexity, maintainability, and scalability in an event-driven AWS architecture. **About the author**: Information Technology Architect @ NOS SGPS. **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/in/pedrojhenriques/ **Duration**: 30 minutes \*\*\* **Speaker**: João Folgado **Language**: English **Title**: From PDF to Chatbot: A Serverless RAG Journey with AWS and MongoDB Atlas **About the author**: Software Engineer @ ABC Glofox **Abstract**: What does it take to turn a pile of PDFs into an intelligent, tenant-aware chatbot -- without managing a single server? In this session, we share the journey of building FitBot, an AI assistant for gym chains that answers questions about schedules, pricing, and policies using only the gym's own documents. We explore how Amazon Textract extracts content, how Step Functions orchestrate the pipeline, how MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores and retrieves embeddings, and how Bedrock Agents tie it all together into a conversational experience. We also dive into the practical challenges: multi-tenancy isolation, incremental document updates, and keeping infrastructure costs near zero with a fully event-driven architecture. **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jo%C3%A3o-folgado-393717255/ **Duration**: 30 minutes \*\*\* **Speaker**: **João Antunes** & **João Mendes** **Language**: English **Title**: Outbox Meets MongoDB: No Event Left Behind **About the author**: Lead architects **Abstract**: Distributed systems are built with failure in mind, but it's surprisingly easy to lose consistency when things don't go as planned. A service crashes, a message broker is unavailable, or a network call times out. What happens to your data and events then? In this session, we'll walk through a typical AWS event-driven architecture, explore where failures can happen, and discuss the problems they can cause. We'll then see how the transactional outbox pattern, implemented with OutboxKit and MongoDB, helps reliably bridge the gap between data changes and event publishing. Along the way, we'll share practical lessons, trade-offs, and tips for building more resilient distributed systems. **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/in/joaofbantunes/ & https://www.linkedin.com/in/joaopcmendes/ **Duration**: 30 minutes \*\*\* **Speaker**: **Rodolfo Cardoso** **Language**: English **Title**: MongoDB + OutSystems + AWS: From Document Data to Scalable Agentic Experiences **About the author**: Lead Solution Architect @ OutSystems **Abstract**: Modern applications increasingly rely on AI, cloud-native architectures, and flexible data models. In this session, we’ll explore how OutSystems, MongoDB, and AWS work together to accelerate the development of intelligent, scalable applications. Through a live demonstration, we’ll showcase OutSystems’ new MongoDB connector, enabling developers to seamlessly connect to MongoDB databases and leverage document-based data within low-code applications. We’ll also explore how this integration can serve as the foundation for building modern AI-powered and agentic experiences, combining the agility of OutSystems with the scalability of MongoDB and the capabilities of AWS. **LinkedIn**: https://www.linkedin.com/in/rtcardoso/ **Duration**: 30 minutes

title: Story of Building Something Bigger Than a Business
description: About the event: For entrerpreneurs, product managers, designers, frontend engineers, founders, and anyone interested. Anyone interested in Product or trying to get into Product Management is welcome. **How curiosity, relationships, and execution created a platform for urban innovation—and what's next.** Building a successful business isn't just about having expertise—it's about solving real problems, building meaningful relationships, and continuously evolving. In this session, you'll hear the journey behind **CitiesFirst**: how a consulting practice grew into a global platform connecting leaders across cities, transportation, technology, and academia. Our speaker will share practical lessons from building a niche consultancy, establishing credibility, winning clients, launching a podcast that became a powerful networking engine, and expanding into international partnerships and events. Together, we'll explore: * How to identify and build around a real market problem * Lessons learned from growing a consulting business * Why relationships consistently outperform traditional marketing * How content can become a strategic asset for business growth * The evolution from consultancy to community and global platform * What's next: AI-powered advisory services, executive education, digital products, and new ways to connect urban innovation leaders Rather than ending with a traditional Q&A, we'll finish with an interactive discussion about the future of project management, entrepreneurship, and urban innovation. Bring your ideas, challenges, and questions—we'll build the conversation together. Whether you're a project manager, consultant, entrepreneur, public sector leader, or simply interested in building products and communities that create real impact, this session will leave you with practical insights and fresh perspectives on turning ideas into lasting value. About our speaker: Scott Shepard is an award-winning urban planner, entrepreneur, author, educator, and global thought leader at the intersection of AI, Urbanism, Mobility, and Decarbonization. He coined the term #CitiesFirst to describe a future-forward, interdisciplinary approach to urban innovation and climate resilience. As Founder & CEO of CitiesFirst Advisors + Podcast and Author of #CitiesFirst: Urbanism & Mobility in the Post-COVID City, Scott brings a unique, systems-level view to climate tech, infratech and proptech ecosystems. He serves on the board of Green Mobility Magazine, Lecturer at Istituto Europeo di Design (IED) and Founding Member & Advisor at Urban AI. Scott is a sought-after speaker at major global forums—Tomorrow.Mobility World Congress, ITS World Congress, IAA MOBILITY, TRB, MOVE, and many more—sharing insights on sustainable cities, future mobility, and digital infrastructure. He's delivered guest lectures at top institutions including Dartmouth, UC San Diego, Coventry University, and advised leading think tanks like Fraunhofer and 2b AHEAD. His thought leadership has been widely featured and cited by organizations such as the UN ILO, European Investment Bank, UITP, NIH, and Financial Times, and published in Intelligent Transport, SmartCitiesWorld, Planetizen, Zag Daily, and others.
